thread:
maria: Heads up — saw TTFT spike on the /v1/chat/stream route around 08:12 UTC. decode time stayed flat, but kernel attribution shows a bigger handoff in the kernel queue. Anyone else see this?
kevin: I saw a small bump too, looks correlated with a batcher change rolled last night (microbatching tweak). Can you paste the dashboard slice?
maria: Screenshot attached (will upload) but main numbers: TTFT median +28ms, decode median +3ms, kernel time +25ms. KV cache hit-rate unchanged.
samir: hmm could be batcher reordering causing extra kernel swaps. We measure kernel handoff as 'kernel_queue_ms' in rt-token-trace. What does the per-token trace look like?
anya: Quick query I ran: `SELECT percentile(token_ttft, 50), percentile(token_decode,50), percentile(kernel_queue_ms,50) FROM token_traces WHERE route='/v1/chat/stream' AND ts > now()-1h` gave 118/93/20 — that 25ms delta matches.
kevin: That suggests kernel_queue_ms moved up. Could be a hot path in kernel selection where we probe the microkernel fallback more frequently now. Any recent change to kernel-selector heuristics?
maria: @samir you touched the kernel selector last sprint right? I remember a change to prefer fused-kernel for short sequences, and fallback probing every Nth batch.
samir: Yup, I added a probing flag to fallback to fallback-kernel every 64th request to validate perf. Looks like sampling frequency accidentally set to 2 for some hosts due to a config bug in rollout.
liz: Oof. That explains sudden kernel handoffs. If fallback kernel has slower dispatch, TTFT will show up without decode changing. We should revert sampling to 64 and then re-run.
kevin: Agreed. Quick mitigation: set env var `KERNEL_PROBE_FREQ=64` on the affected pool, and push a small deploy.
infra-bot: deploy started: rollout/rtd-batcher-fix -> canary on pool-gamma (3 hosts).
maria: Reverted probe freq on pool-gamma. Watching the metrics.
anya: While rolling back, can we add a per-route tag to the kernel-attribution metric? Right now it's per-host and aggregate; per-route would let us slice by /v1/chat/stream vs /v1/embeddings.
samir: Good idea. We can add `route` label to token-level gauge `kernel_time_ms` and `kernel_queue_ms`. Cost is extra metrics cardinality; we should limit to top 20 routes by traffic.
kevin: Proposal: create a derived metric `kernel_time_by_route` that only ingests when route in top_routes_set. Also add sampling flag to include full route for a small sample (1%) for outlier detection.
liz: Also add a boolean label `probe_hit=true/false` so we can separate probe-induced handoffs.
maria: Results: after the revert, TTFT median fell back to baseline in ~6 minutes. kernel_queue_ms median dropped 22ms.
kevin: Perf regression root cause = misconfigured probe freq causing frequent fallback kernel selection. Action items: (1) add protective validation to rollout code to prevent probe freq < 8, (2) implement route-limited kernel_time_by_route metric, (3) add probe_hit label.
anya: I'll open a dashboard PR with token-level breakdown panels: TTFT vs decode vs kernel_queue, and heatmap for probe_hit.
samir: I'll send a small rollout patch that validates probe freq and marks hosts with `probe_hit` in traces so metrics pick it up.
infra-bot: deploy success: rollout/rtd-batcher-fix -> pool-gamma completed.
maria: thanks all. follow-up: can we add an alert if kernel_queue_ms p95 increases >10ms over baseline for any top route? That would've caught this faster.
kevin: +1. I'll add a per-route alert linked to the new metric set and create an automated runbook entry.
liz: And let's add a nightly job to sample token traces and produce a weekly TTFT-vs-decode delta report.
maria: Great. TL;DR in #eng-status after lunch. :thumbsup:
